description: Pins protocol::encode_quick_unlock_blob_raw + protocol::decode_quick_unlock_blob byte mapping for the MYQ1 vault.quickunlock device-local credential codec (MYND-329; §9.14). The blob wraps a THIRD copy of root_key (32 bytes) under a provider-supplied wrap_key — the codec is PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC: it never runs Argon2id (the PIN→wrap_key derivation is pinned separately in the argon2id family as input_path 'quickunlock-pin'), so vectors supply wrap_key DIRECTLY as a fixed fixture. provider_kind (0x01 biometric / 0x02 PIN) and account_number_hash both bind via aad_quick_unlock_blob (AAD role 'quick-unlock-blob'); there is NO HKDF SubkeyRole (a root_key-derived KEK would be circular). ciphertext_len is the fixed constant 64 (root_key 32 + CTX tag 32), so there is no size cap / ciphertext_len_overflow case. 12 cases: 2 encrypt (biometric + PIN) + 1 decrypt_ok + 3 decrypt_aead_fail (tag-tamper + cross-vault + provider_kind-flip, all non-distinguishing per §6.4) + 6 parse_fail (one per distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject). Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_quick_unlock_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/quick_unlock_blob.rs).

cases.description: Encode under the biometric provider (provider_kind=0x01, e.g. macOS Keychain). pin_salt is all-zero (unused by a non-PIN provider but still a header field). The wrap_key is the provider's symmetric secret, supplied directly. Expected blob = 50-byte header + 32-byte root_key ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag = 114 bytes.

Encode under the PIN provider (provider_kind=0x02). pin_salt (0xab×16) is the Argon2id salt the desktop layer used to derive wrap_key from the PIN; it is stored in the public header so the salt can be read back before decode. The wrap_key here is the already-derived 32-byte key (the Argon2id step is pinned separately in the argon2id family). Expected blob = 114 bytes.

Round-trip the biometric blob back to the wrapped root_key under the matching wrap_key + account_number_hash. Proves the decoder's header parse + AEAD unwrap reconstruct the exact 32-byte root_key (the third wrapped copy).

Take the biometric blob and flip the final byte (inside the 32-byte CTX commitment tag) via XOR 0xFF. The decoder MUST surface a non-distinguishing CannotDecrypt. Same observable outcome as the cross-vault and provider-flip cases (spec §6.4).
cases.informational_tamper_description: final byte (inside CTX tag) flipped via XOR 0xFF

cases.description: Take the intact biometric blob but decrypt under a DIFFERENT account_number_hash (0x11×16 instead of 0x7c×16). aad_quick_unlock_blob binds the account hash, so the AAD differs and AEAD verification fails — a credential from vault A cannot unwrap vault B's root_key. Collapses to the same CannotDecrypt; ports MUST NOT distinguish.
cases.informational_tamper_description: intact blob decrypted under wrong account_number_hash (0x11×16)

cases.description: Take the valid biometric blob (provider_kind=0x01) and flip the provider_kind byte (offset 5) to 0x02 (PIN). Both values are registered, so this passes the structural provider_kind check — but provider_kind is bound into the AAD (§9.14.3), so the AEAD verification fails. This is a decrypt_aead_fail, NOT a parse_fail: it proves a biometric-minted credential cannot be reinterpreted as a PIN credential.
First byte of the MYQ1 magic corrupted to 'X'. Rejected at offset 0 before any decryption (magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline, §9.14.1).
protocol_version byte (offset 4) set to 0x02 instead of 0x01. A v0.1 decoder rejects an unknown protocol version before decrypting.

provider_kind byte (offset 5) set to 0x09 — not a registered provider (only 0x01 biometric / 0x02 PIN exist). Rejected structurally before decryption. Contrast the provider-kind-flip decrypt_aead_fail case, where the flipped value (0x02) IS registered and so reaches the AAD-bound AEAD stage.

ciphertext_len field (offset 46..50) set to 65 instead of the fixed 64 (root_key 32 + CTX tag 32). The quick-unlock blob always wraps exactly one root_key, so any other length is rejected before the AEAD stage (there is no variable-size cap here, unlike vault-search/indices).
Only the 4-byte MYQ1 magic, no room for the 50-byte header. Rejected before any field read.
Valid header advertising ciphertext_len = 64, but the blob is one byte shorter than header + 64. Rejected before the AEAD stage.
